Name: persona_belief_contamination
Title: Whose Belief Is It? Separating a Persona's False Beliefs from the Model's Own Inside LLMs
Short Hypothesis: When an LLM role-plays a persona that holds a factually false belief the model itself does not endorse (e.g., a flat-earther, a 19th-century physician), the model maintains a persona-belief representation that is partially distinct from its own-belief representation, but the two are entangled such that adopting the persona *contaminates* the model's own internal belief. We hypothesize both beliefs are simultaneously and linearly decodable, that the degree of own-belief contamination is measurable and predicts factual errors after role-play, and that a 'belief-ownership' direction can be steered to insulate the model's own belief from the persona's. The centerpiece is contamination, not simultaneous decoding: adopting a persona that holds a real-world-false belief shifts the model's OWN internal factual belief, this shift predicts own-voice factual leakage after role-play, and a belief-ownership direction can insulate the own-belief while preserving faithful role-play. Contamination is defined and tested apart from mere instruction-following, answer-format persistence, and activation of a generic persona/assistant axis.
Related Work: Prior work shows LLMs linearly represent self/other beliefs for Theory-of-Mind (Language Models Represent Beliefs of Self and Others 2024; Brittle Minds 2024) and can steer ToM performance, but the 'self' and 'other' beliefs there are ordinary beliefs either agent could hold about a story world, not cases where the persona holds a belief the model *knows to be factually false about the real world*. Persona work (Assistant Axis 2026; Persona Selection Model 2026) shows a persona/Assistant direction governs behavior and 'persona drift', and self-recognition work isolates a 'self' vector, but neither tracks whether adopting a false-believing persona corrupts the model's own factual belief representation. Neuroscience (Thornton & Mitchell 2019; agent-specific learning signals 2018) finds humans represent their own states more distinctly than others'. We combine these: we introduce a controlled 'persona-vs-self false-belief' paradigm and treat contamination of the model's own belief by a persona as a measurable, localizable, and steerable phenomenon distinct from ToM belief decoding. Unlike prior descriptive persona-drift work, we operationalize contamination at the level of the model's *own factual belief representation* and provide a causal insulation intervention. Delta against the two closest baselines: ToM self/other decoding (Beliefs of Self and Others 2024) concerns beliefs either agent could hold in a story — it would not flag that the 'other' belief is false about the real world, nor predict own-voice leakage; persona-drift/assistant-axis work (2026) tracks behavioral drift along a persona direction — it would attribute our effect to generic persona activation, which we rule out by controlling for assistant-axis magnitude and by a no-persona matched-false-statement control. The novelty is the false-real-world-belief setting plus own-voice leakage prediction and causal insulation, not linear probing. Released artifact: a persona-vs-self false-belief benchmark, a contamination metric, and an insulation steering method.
Abstract: Large language models routinely role-play personas, and users increasingly ask them to speak 'as' a flat-earther, a medieval doctor, or a user who believes a false premise. This raises a mechanistic question with direct safety relevance: when the model adopts a persona that holds a belief the model itself does not endorse, does it keep a clean separation between the persona's belief and its own, or does the persona's false belief contaminate the model's own internal representation? Prior Theory-of-Mind interpretability work decodes self/other beliefs, but only for beliefs either agent could hold in a story; prior persona work characterizes 'persona drift' behaviorally. We study the intersection: personas whose factual beliefs conflict with the model's own knowledge. We build a controlled dataset of real-world item-state facts paired with personas that (dis)believe them, and elicit the model to answer as the persona and then, in a matched clean context, answer in its own voice. We train linear probes on frozen open-weight models (Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B) to simultaneously decode (i) the persona's belief and (ii) the model's own belief, measure their geometric relationship, and quantify a 'contamination' score: the degree to which the model's own-belief representation shifts toward a false persona belief. We test whether contamination predicts post-role-play factual errors, localize the responsible heads via activation patching, and derive a 'belief-ownership' steering direction (contrastive activation addition from own-voice vs. persona-voice activations) to test whether we can insulate the model's own belief while preserving faithful role-play. Metrics: joint probe accuracy/AUROC, subspace angle, contamination score, contamination-error AUROC, patching effect sizes, post-role-play factual accuracy, role-play faithfulness, and perplexity. So what: post-role-play own-voice factual leakage is a concrete deployment risk in customer-support role-play, educational debate, and jailbreak personas; if contamination exists, practitioners should benchmark and steer against it or avoid certain persona patterns, and if it does not, current persona use is safer than feared. We estimate the effect size in realistic multi-turn chat, include at least one instruction-tuned/API model for behavioral validation of external relevance, and release the benchmark, metric, and insulation method.
Experiments:
Experiment 1 (H1 — persona-belief and model-own-belief are simultaneously linearly decodable): Data: built from scratch, 5,000 real-world facts the target models reliably know (verified by >= 90% correct own-voice answering), each with matched OWN, PERSONA-CONCORDANT, and PERSONA-DISCORDANT (false-believing persona) contexts, plus comprehension checks; split 70/15/15 by fact. Model: Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B, frozen; trainable component only two logistic-regression probes (persona-belief, own-belief) on residual activations at the state token, per layer; 5 seeds. Systems compared: each probe vs. shuffled-label control. Decisive metric first: test AUROC of each probe at best layer. Convincing: both >= 0.80, controls 0.50 +/- 0.05, on >=2 of 3 models. Indecision band: 0.60-0.70 for either probe is weak. Negative: own-belief probe < 0.60 means own-belief is not separately readable and contamination cannot be measured.

Experiment 2 (H1 — own-belief is represented more distinctly than persona-belief; the two are partially distinct but entangled): Decisive metric first: subspace angle between own-belief and persona-belief directions, plus own-vs-persona probe-margin difference; secondary: projected-out decodability. Convincing: angle in (20,70) degrees (partial distinctness) and own-belief margin significantly larger than persona-belief (paired test, p<0.05). Indecision band: angle < 20 degrees (near-collinear) or > 80 degrees (fully separate) each falsify the 'partially distinct but entangled' claim in opposite directions and are reported as such. Negative for the distinctness sub-claim: no margin difference.

Experiment 3 (H2 — adopting a discordant persona contaminates own-belief, and contamination predicts errors): Decisive metric first: contamination score = shift of the own-belief probe toward the false persona value in the DISCORDANT vs. OWN condition; secondary: AUROC using contamination to predict errors on the step-out-of-character own-voice leakage probe, vs. a log-prob baseline. Convincing: mean contamination significantly > 0 (bootstrap CI excludes 0) and contamination-error AUROC >= 0.70, >= 0.05 above log-prob. Indecision band: contamination CI includes 0, or AUROC 0.60-0.70, is weak. Negative: contamination ~ 0 and AUROC <= 0.60 means personas do not corrupt own-belief.

Experiment 4 (H2 — localization): Activation patching to find heads mediating contamination; compare to persona/Assistant-axis and self-recognition directions from prior work. Decisive metric first: fraction of contamination recovered by top heads. Convincing: reproducible <= 20-head set recovers >= 50%. Indecision band: diffuse = distributed. Negative: no head > 20%.

Experiment 5 (H3 — a belief-ownership direction insulates own-belief without breaking role-play): Build an ownership CAA vector (own-voice minus persona-voice activations); during discordant role-play steer toward 'own' (alpha 2/4/8% residual norm). Systems compared: ownership steering vs. random vs. persona-axis steering. Decisive metric first: reduction in own-voice contamination/error; secondary: role-play faithfulness rate (must stay >= 90% of unsteered), MMLU-subset, perplexity. Convincing: >= 10-point error reduction with faithfulness preserved and perplexity rise < 10%; random < 3 points. Indecision band: 3-10 points suggestive. Negative: < 3 points beyond random, or faithfulness collapses, means no clean insulation handle.

Experiment 6 (H1,H3 — generalization): Apply frozen probes/steering across fact domains, persona types, jailbreak personas, and multi-turn role-play. Decisive metric first: transfer AUROC and error-reduction retention. Convincing: >= 0.70 and half the effect retained. Indecision band: 0.60-0.70. Negative: <= 0.60.

Experiment 7 (H2 — discourse-carryover controls and external validation): Separates genuine own-belief contamination from instruction-following/carryover and checks larger models. Data: the discordant items re-run with a hard context reset, paraphrased and delayed own-voice probes, irrelevant intervening turns, and a no-persona control that states the same false content without a persona; plus a behavioral-only replication on one instruction-tuned/API model. Decisive metric first: own-voice error rate in the discordant condition minus the no-persona matched-false control, after context reset and delay; secondary: assistant-axis magnitude as a covariate, and the API-model behavioral leakage rate. Convincing: contamination survives context reset/delay and exceeds the no-persona control (bootstrap CI excludes 0) and is not explained by assistant-axis magnitude. Indecision band: effect present only without reset is reported as carryover, not contamination. Negative: no excess over the no-persona control means the effect is instruction-following.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Contamination could reflect the model simply obeying the discordant instruction rather than a corrupted internal own-belief; the matched OWN/discordant design, the explicit step-out-of-character leakage probe, and comprehension checks help disentangle instruction-following from genuine belief contamination. Persona-belief and own-belief may not be cleanly linearly separable or may be layer/model-specific; we report layerwise results with control tasks and use joint probes. The two belief directions may be more entangled than hypothesized, in which case the finding becomes a characterization of that entanglement (still informative and safety-relevant). Belief-ownership steering could degrade fluency or break faithful role-play (making the model refuse to stay in character); we monitor perplexity, role-play faithfulness, use small magnitudes, and separate 'reduce contamination' from 'break persona'. Personas whose beliefs are genuinely near the model's uncertainty (contested facts) confound the contamination signal; we restrict the core analysis to facts the model reliably knows. Results may not transfer to very large closed models. 'Own belief' is validated with multiple probes/tasks showing convergence beyond immediate response policy, and probes use delexicalized/paraphrased prompts with persona-template splits so they cannot exploit surface form. Localization includes random-head and known-assistant/persona-direction controls to show selected heads are belief-specific rather than generic role-play heads. Steering faithfulness is judged with semantic role-play rubrics, not only perplexity. The core analysis is restricted to facts the model reliably knows so contested-fact uncertainty does not confound contamination.
